To generate an answer again, set `trigger: "regenerate-message"` and optionally `messageId`; the conversation is cut back to that message (by default, the last answer) and the answer is generated again, and a failed regeneration keeps the previous answer. An ordinary submission containing any message ID already in accepted history returns `409 message_id_conflict` before model or tool work, including when its text changes or its batch also contains new IDs. Regeneration can reuse existing IDs. Returns `409 session_busy` while another turn is running or a tool approval is waiting for a decision. A turn that stopped responding keeps the session busy for up to a minute. Once it is clear that the turn stopped, the request returns `409 session_turn_unresponsive` with a `Retry-After` header that says when to send it again. Send exactly one of `messages` or `promptId`; `variables` is allowed only with `promptId`. The answer streams back as an AI SDK UI message stream. A failure before the stream starts returns a JSON error. Once the stream has started, a failure arrives as an error chunk; the turn still counts toward usage, and the conversation is left as it was.

post.description: Creates a task: a saved prompt your agent runs in the background. With a `schedule`, the task runs by itself; without one, it runs only when you start it. Send `submit: true` to start a run right away, which returns `202 Accepted` with the run's ID in `runId`; otherwise you get `201 Created` and `runId` is `null`. Keys are separate for tenant-wide access and each scoped user. Without a key, each request creates another task. The platform-managed agent cannot run tasks.

Every final status sets `finishedAt` and lets the task start another run.
